new_cards.title: Fault-injection campaign on the safety functions
new_cards.purpose: Show in the model that each detected failure reaches its safe state in time
new_cards.description: From the FMEA (G3-FME), the integration engineer injects each failure mode that the design claims to detect into the system model with Simulink Fault Analyzer: a stuck, noisy or frozen sensor, a lost scan, a lost CAN link, an ESC fault, a brake that does not engage, a stale IMU, a lost RC link. For each fault it checks that the safe state is reached within the reaction time of the concept, and records the margin. A failure that does not reach its safe state is a nonconformance.

new_cards.title: Safety case
new_cards.purpose: A reasoned argument, with its evidence, that the robot is acceptably safe for mowing within its envelope
new_cards.description: The functional safety engineer writes the safety case: a structured argument, in goal structuring notation, that each safety goal is met. Its evidence: the hazard log, the safety concept, the FMEA and fault trees, the fault-injection results, the verification campaigns in simulation, on the bench and in the field, and the field-test records. It lists the residual risks and the operating limits, the CR-001 envelope among them. The independent reviewer assesses it, and the owner accepts the residual risks.

risks.risk: The drive cannot absorb the energy at CCL 0

new_cards.title: A controlled stop without skidding (later phase)
new_cards.purpose: Win back the 20 deg design slope for the full-tank sprayer
new_cards.description: CR-001 limits the full-tank sprayer to about 18.5 deg, because a brakes-locked stop skids the tracks and can tip the robot over its front. A controlled stop that does not skid, with the drive braking the robot to standstill before the brakes close, would raise the safe speed and could restore the 20 deg slope (the structure engineer's proposal on card G2-DSC). Without regeneration (a full battery, CCL 0), the drive needs another way to absorb the energy, such as a braking resistor: a hardware question for the owner and the supplier.

criteria: G2-DSC closed
The owner's view on a braking resistor or another energy path

criteria: A stop without skidding shown in the full vehicle model on 20 deg with the full-tank sprayer

new_cards.title: Cybersecurity threat analysis (later phase)
new_cards.purpose: Know how the robot's links could be misused, and what protects them
new_cards.description: The robot is driven by RC, takes corrections over LTE (NTRIP), and links the MCU and the companion over CAN. No one has yet asked how these links could be jammed, spoofed or misused. The electronics and comms engineer runs a threat analysis of the RC link, the LTE and NTRIP link, the CAN buses and the companion's services, rates each threat and proposes the protections. A threat that could defeat a safety function goes into the hazard log. The reference standard (IEC 62443, or one for agricultural machinery) is the owner's to confirm.

role.title: Functional safety engineer
role.does: Leads the safety life cycle: the safety plan, the hazard log, the functional safety concept, the FMEA and fault trees, and the safety case. Sets the required performance levels; checks that each safety requirement is met and verified; works with the subsystem engineers who design the safety functions; escalates a safety gap to the owner.
role.never: Designs or changes the safety functions it assesses: the subsystem engineers do, which keeps the assessment independent. Edits the models or the code. Closes a safety gap that needs a hardware change without the owner.
role.owns: docs/safety/: the safety plan, the hazard log, the safety concept, the FMEA and fault trees, the safety case; the Safety Analysis Manager files
